scene.source: bell ring frequency from field.interface.acoustics.ring_frequency (f=v_L/(pi*d), the same formula the acoustics() Materia verb cites for bells); impact energy partition and click frequency from field.interface.impact (Johnson-Thornton/Hertz contact mechanics, the SAME model record_fall's bounce restitution already uses) -- not invented from raw kinetic energy; stone impact resolved by the engine's own pairwise contact solver (dynamics/collision.py), not scripted. The bell hangs from a REAL modeled 3-link suspension chain (RevoluteJoint hinges, dynamics/joints.py), weld-anchored only at the top to a fixed world point -- a standard rigid-body world anchor idealization, the same kind as an unmodeled floor/ground plane (this scene stages no wall/ceiling geometry, so the anchor is not a physically modeled ceiling or room structure), not a Plug (no support disclosure needed: the chain itself, not a hand-wave, is what holds the bell up). CHOSEN: bell material/size, stone mass/material, and observer distance = {'bell_material': 'iron', 'bell_diameter_m': 0.15, 'stone_mass_kg': 0.2, 'stone_material': 'granite', 'observer_distance_m': 50.0} (checked: materia/translator.py strike_bell routing (no slot extraction yet for tool/stone size or observer distance from free text); the request named neither a bell size/material, a stone mass, nor an observer distance, so these are this function's own defaults, not measured/cited values). CHOSEN: bell height-to-diameter proportion = 0.85 (checked: no cited casting on file for a specific bell; a typical bell silhouette is somewhat taller than its rim radius; picked for a legible shape, not measured). CHOSEN: stone start offset from the bell rim and drop height = {'rim_frac': 0.7, 'drop_height_over_stone_r': 4.0} (checked: no cited throw trajectory for this demo; a short drop near the rim gives a real nonzero impact velocity without a long empty-fall simulation window). CHOSEN: suspension chain: link count, total length, and per-link wire radius (replaces the prior bare world-weld at the bell's own center of mass) = {'n_links': 3, 'chain_length_m': 0.09, 'link_wire_radius_m': 0.00375} (checked: no cited casting/mounting hardware exists for a specific bell of this size; radiance/theaters.py's room() ceiling proportion (H = max(3.2*r, 0.65)) checked for an ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE sense of 'how far above the content a ceiling sits', but not applied directly -- theaters.py stages z-up static Deckard scenes, this trajectory scene is the dynamics engine's own y-up convention; chain length picked short (a hand-bell hung close to its mount, not a long drop) so the assembly still reads as 'a bell on a chain' on screen; wire radius kept thin relative to the bell so chain mass stays a small fraction of the bell's own, as a real suspension chain would). CHOSEN: bell ring decay time constant = 2.5 (checked: no material Q-factor table on file for bell decay; a several-second ring-down is typical for a struck metal bell; not measured from field.interface data (SIMPLIFIED_MODEL -- real decay is material- and mode-dependent)). CHOSEN: bell strike amplitude vs. reference DISSIPATED impact energy (impact_energy_partition's E_dissipated_J, not raw kinetic energy) = {'reference_dissipated_energy_j': 0.1, 'min_amplitude': 0.05} (checked: field.interface.impact.impact_energy_partition (real Johnson-Thornton energy conservation) for the ENERGY input; no cited energy-to-SPL/radiation-efficiency curve on file for the SCALE; amplitude scales monotonically with the real dissipated energy but the absolute loudness scale itself is not measured (SIMPLIFIED_MODEL)). SIMPLIFIED_MODEL: single sustained vibrational mode synthesized (the impact click is reported as a number, not a second audio layer), sphere-approximated bell collision envelope, inverse-square-only atmospheric propagation, chain hinges share one swing axis (planar swing only, not a full universal-joint chain).

acoustics.model: inverse-square (spherical spreading) from a 1 m reference only; frequency-dependent atmospheric absorption NOT modeled (SIMPLIFIED_MODEL)
